questions.question: Ch1 Q1. What does the term "Enterprise" refer to in the context of enterprise management?
options: A for-profit business company that produces services or products
An educational institution offering degree programs
A non-profit organization focused on social welfare
A government agency responsible for regulatory oversight
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch1 Q2. Which of the following best defines "Management"?
options: The use of technology to automate business operations
The coordination and organization of resources, people, and processes to achieve specific goals
The process of producing goods and services for customers
The creation of financial reports for stakeholders
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch1 Q3. Enterprise Management is best described as:
options: A method of managing only the financial aspects of a business
The systematic approach used to oversee all activities within a business to achieve objectives
A government framework for regulating businesses
A strategy focused exclusively on marketing and customer acquisition
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

options: People, capital, materials, space, and time
Marketing, sales, advertising, branding, and pricing
Inputs, outputs, feedback, process, and control
Planning, organizing, leading, controlling, and staffing
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch1 Q5. In enterprise management, the products generated by a business are referred to as:
options: Resources
Inputs
Outputs
Assets
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch1 Q6. Which of the following is an example of an enterprise mentioned in the text?
options: The United Nations
Walmart
The World Health Organization
Harvard University
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch1 Q7. Which of the following best explains why creativity and innovation are increasingly demanded in today's business environment?
options: Governments require businesses to innovate for tax benefits
Technological advancements have made innovation unnecessary EM MCQ BANK
The business environment is increasingly competitive
Customers prefer traditional products and services
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch1 Q8. Raw materials, labour, equipment, and technology are examples of:
options: Products
Resources plans
Inputs
Outputs

options: Implementing technology and marketing campaigns only
Making strategic decisions and coordinating resources only
Only managing personnel and finances
Making strategic decisions, coordinating resources, managing personnel, and implementing processes

questions.question: Ch1 Q10. Which statement is TRUE about an enterprise?

An enterprise is created and operated by a government body
An enterprise can range from a small business to a multinational corporation
An enterprise can only be a small business

options: Seven
Five
Eight
Six

questions.question: Ch1 Q12. Which core area of enterprise management is described as "the backbone of every enterprise management plan"?
options: Strategic management
Human resource management
Financial management
Operations management

questions.question: Ch1 Q13. Which of the following is a key responsibility of Financial Management?
options: Recruiting and training employees
Designing and launching new marketing campaigns
Developing customer service policies
Managing cash flow, debt, liabilities, and equity
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

options: Recruiting and compensating employees
Converting inputs into outputs as effectively as possible
Managing customer complaints and feedback

options: The importance of financial planning
The breadth and interdependencies of the business environment
The need for employee training and development
The role of technology in business automation

options: Conducting financial audits and preparing reports
Implementing cybersecurity measures
Managing employee performance reviews
Identifying target audience groups and decision-makers
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch1 Q17. Customer Relationship Management (CRM) primarily aims to:
options: Develop new technology infrastructure
Enhance the customer's overall experience
Maximize profits through aggressive sales tactics
Manage internal employee communications

options: Conducting SWOT analysis
Setting financial budgets for the company
Recruiting and onboarding new employees
Managing customer complaint tickets in a timely manner

questions.question: Ch1 Q19. According to Edwin Flippo, Human Resource Management includes:
options: Strategic resource allocation and IT planning
Financial planning and investment management
Planning, organizing, directing, and controlling of human resources
Product development and innovation management

options: Developing new product lines for customers
Overseeing business data management including storage, maintenance, and protection
Managing supplier relationships and procurement
Conducting market research and competitive analysis
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

options: Creating branding strategies for new products
Creating, implementing, and administering effective operations systems and practices
Designing employee performance appraisal processes
Developing financial forecasting models
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch1 Q22. Which of the following best describes the role of IT Management regarding cybersecurity?
options: Developing advertising strategies to protect brand reputation
Managing customer data to improve sales conversions
Implementing cybersecurity and risk management to keep systems safe
Recruiting IT specialists for the marketing department

options: Conducting SWOT analysis for strategic planning
Analyzing competitors' pricing strategies
Developing performance management plans and succession planning
Overseeing network infrastructure and software systems

options: An HR team and recruitment platforms EM MCQ BANK
An effective marketing team and advertising budget
A reliable accounting team and financial tools
An operations team and production equipment

options: Conducting SWOT analysis to identify threats and growth opportunities
Maximizing advertising spend on new products
Outsourcing all non-core business functions
Reducing the workforce to cut costs
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch1 Q26. Which of the following is identified as a key challenge for businesses in the 21st century?
options: Rapid technological advancements disrupting industries
Decreased reliance on digital systems
Simplification of regulatory requirements
Reduction in global competition

options: Reduce investment in online platforms
Lead organizations through initiatives to optimize processes and enhance customer experiences
Replace all human employees with automated systems
Focus solely on traditional business models
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch1 Q28. The modern workforce described in the chapter includes:
options: Only full-time employees working in a single office
Only highly skilled technical professionals
Employees from a single cultural background
Multiple generations, remote workers, and gig economy participants
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch1 Q29. Talent Management challenges primarily involve:
options: Developing new IT infrastructure
Finding and retaining top talent while addressing the skills gap
Finding the right advertising agency for marketing campaigns
Managing supplier contracts and procurement negotiations
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch1 Q30. Which 21st-century challenge requires managers to ensure ethical decision-making and drive corporate social responsibility initiatives?
options: Ethical and social responsibility
Agility and adaptability
Data privacy and security
Change management
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch1 Q31. Which of the following best defines "Agility and Adaptability" as a business challenge?
options: Avoiding change in organizational structure
Reducing investments in technology to control costs
Fostering organizational agility to respond effectively to market shifts and disruptions
The ability to maintain the same business strategy for decades
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch1 Q32. Data Privacy and Security challenges require managers to:
options: Reduce reliance on digital systems entirely EM MCQ BANK
Prioritize marketing data collection over legal compliance
Share all customer data with third parties for better service
Implement robust cybersecurity measures and comply with data protection regulations
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch1 Q33. Which challenge deals with implementing new strategies, technologies, or organizational structures?
options: Work-life balance
Talent management
Change management
Globalization
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

options: Increase work hours to improve productivity
Prioritize employee well-being and create a supportive work environment
Focus on shareholder profits over employee satisfaction
Eliminate remote working options
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch1 Q35. Globalization affects businesses primarily by:
options: Reducing the need to understand different cultural environments
Limiting access to international markets
Increasing competition from both domestic and international players
Simplifying regulatory compliance
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch1 Q36. Which of the following best describes the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on businesses?
options: AI is only relevant to large multinational corporations
AI has eliminated all operational challenges for businesses
AI has reduced the need for data analytics
AI is one of the emerging technologies managers must adapt to and leverage effectively
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch1 Q37. A business that struggles to find employees with the right qualifications for new technology roles is facing which challenge?
options: Digital transformation
Data privacy and security
Talent management and skills gap
Work-life balance
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch1 Q38. Which of the following is NOT listed as a 21st-century challenge facing businesses in the chapter?
options: Reduction in customer demand
Globalization and international competition
Changing workforce dynamics
Ethical and social responsibility
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch1 Q39. To successfully navigate 21st-century challenges, managers need to:
options: Resist change and maintain traditional practices
Focus solely on maximizing short-term profits
Continuously update their skills and adopt agile leadership approaches
Eliminate diversity in the workplace
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch1 Q40. Which of the following management areas would be MOST directly responsible for addressing the "Skills Gap" challenge in a business?
options: Information Technology Management EM MCQ BANK
Human Resource Management
Operations Management
Financial Management
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch2 Q1. Operations Management is best defined as:
options: The process of handling legal and regulatory compliance matters
The management of the part of an organization responsible for producing goods and/or services
The management of financial transactions and investments within an organization
The coordination of marketing campaigns and promotional activities
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch2 Q2. An Operating System is defined as:
options: A physical infrastructure of a manufacturing plant
A software program that controls computer hardware and networks
A configuration of resources combined for the provision of goods or services
A set of rules and procedures governing employee behavior
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch2 Q3. Which of the following is the PRIMARY concern of Operations Management that distinguishes it from other functions like marketing and finance?
options: Conversion of inputs into outputs using physical resources
Strategic planning and long-term decision making
Maximizing customer satisfaction through after-sales service
Managing human resources and employee relations
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch2 Q4. Which of the following are examples of inputs used in the transformation process?
options: Capital, labour, and information
Feedback, control, outputs, and quality
Products, services, profits, and customer satisfaction
Planning, organizing, leading, and controlling
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch2 Q5. In an operating system, "feedback" refers to:
options: Measurements taken at various points in the transformation process and compared with standards
Employee performance reviews conducted annually
Customer complaints submitted after purchasing a product
Financial reports submitted to management at year end
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch2 Q6. Which of the following best describes a "product package"?
options: A combination of goods and services sold together by a company
A financial plan for product development and launch
A bundle of physical goods sold at a discounted price
A marketing strategy used to attract new customers
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch2 Q7. Which of the following is an example of an Operating System?
options: A hospital providing medical services EM MCQ BANK Chapter 2: Operations Management & Its Importance Page 11 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
A SWOT analysis framework
A financial budgeting model
A corporate marketing strategy
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch2 Q8. The goods-service combination in operations is described as:
options: A continuum ranging from primarily goods to primarily service
A fixed ratio of goods to services in every product
An equal balance of goods and services in all businesses
A model only applicable to manufacturing companies
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch2 Q9. Which of the following is listed as an activity under the Scope of Operations Management?
options: Plant layouts and material handling
Advertising and brand management
Recruitment and employee compensation
Financial auditing and reporting
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch2 Q10. "Control" in an operating system means:
options: Managing the financial budget of the operations department
Comparing measurements from the transformation process with established standards to determine if corrective action is needed
Overseeing supplier relationships and procurement activities
Directing employees to follow company policies
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch2 Q11. Which of the following is NOT listed as an activity under Production and Operations Management functions?
options: Materials Management
Sales and Marketing
Location of Facilities
Quality Control
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch2 Q12. Process Design in operations management aims to:
options: Create marketing strategies for new product launches
Develop financial forecasting and budgeting models
Design employee appraisal and performance management systems

questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

Developing marketing plans for new product lines
Managing procurement, storage, and distribution of raw materials and finished goods

Overseeing financial transactions and investment decisions
Managing employee welfare and benefits programs

Advertising budgets and promotional strategies

Production management is a newer concept, while operations management is historical

Production management deals with HR, while operations management deals with finance

A car manufacturing plant
A steel production factory

Operations Management, as it evolved from Production Management
Production Management, as it is more comprehensive

Four
Five
Six

Technostructure
Strategic apex

The hierarchy of authority from strategic apex to front-line supervisors

Operating core

questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

Quality Management
Risk Management
Cost Efficiency

By outsourcing quality checks to third-party vendors

options: Supply Chain Management
Flexibility and Adaptability
Cost Efficiency
Risk Management
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

Outsourcing all research and development activities
Integrating customer feedback, market insights, and technological advancements into product design

questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

options: Reducing product prices regardless of quality
Ensuring timely delivery of products or services meeting quality and quantity expectations
Increasing advertising spend to attract new customers

Speed

questions.question: Ch2 Q39. How does Operations Management interact with Accounting and Finance? EM MCQ BANK Chapter 2: Operations Management & Its Importance Page 15 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: Operations Management works independently without any financial interaction
Accounting and Finance control all operational decisions without input from operations managers
Operations Management decisions have financial implications, requiring close collaboration with accounting and finance
Operations Management only interacts with finance during annual budget reviews
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch2 Q40. In the Hyperstar illustration, keeping inventory levels low contributes to which operations strategy objective?
options: Innovation and Product Development
Quality Management
Flexibility and Adaptability

questions.question: Ch3 Q1. A production system is best defined as:
options: A method used to manage employees in a manufacturing environment
Any method used in industry to create goods and services from various resources
A financial planning tool used to forecast production costs
A quality control framework for monitoring output standards
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch3 Q2. The two main categories of production systems are:
options: Job production and batch production
Manual production and automated production
Large-scale production and small-scale production
Intermittent production system and continuous production system
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch3 Q3. "Intermittent" in the context of a production system means:
options: Something that follows a fixed and predetermined production schedule
Something that operates constantly without any irregularities
Something that starts and stops at irregular intervals
Something that produces standardized goods in large quantities
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch3 Q4. In an intermittent production system, goods are produced:
options: Based on customer orders on a small scale
In large standardized batches for stocking in warehouses
Using fully automated machinery without human involvement
Continuously based on demand forecasts
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch3 Q5. Which of the following is a characteristic of an intermittent production system?
options: Products are highly standardized with no variation
General purpose machines are used that can produce different types of products
Goods are produced on a large scale in anticipation of demand
The flow of production is continuous and uninterrupted
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch3 Q6. Which of the following is NOT a type of intermittent production system?
options: Jobbing production
Project production
Mass production
Batch production
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch3 Q7. The work of a goldsmith making ornaments based on customer orders is an example of:
options: Continuous production system
Mass production system
Intermittent production system
Process production system
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch3 Q8. In an intermittent production system, the sequence of operations: EM MCQ BANK Chapter 3: Types of Production Systems Page 17 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included

Changes as per the design of each product
Is determined only by the production manager
Is fully automated and requires no human input
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

options: Fully automated and continuous
Fixed and predetermined by annual forecasts
Very large scale to meet market-wide demand
Small scale based on individual customer orders
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

The production flow is continuous and uninterrupted
Goods are produced on a large scale for standardized markets
Products are made and stocked in warehouses until demand arises
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

A single complex order or contract to be completed within a given time and estimated cost
Repeat orders from the same customer on a continuous basis
Bulk orders based on demand forecasts for warehouse stocking
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

Manufacturing toothpaste on a large scale
Producing pharmaceuticals in large batches
Construction of airports, dams, and roads
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

options: Production follows a continuous and uninterrupted flow
Resource requirement remains constant throughout the project
Resource requirement is low at the start, increases in the middle, and slows near completion
Routing and scheduling remain fixed throughout the project
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

Due to the complexity and massiveness of the project
Due to the continuous flow of production
Due to lack of customer demand for the product
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

All jobs are performed by a single department
The production schedule is fixed and cannot be changed EM MCQ BANK
All jobs are interrelated and many agencies perform specialized tasks
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch3 Q16. Jobbing production involves:

Continuous production of standardized goods for mass markets
Constructing large infrastructure projects over extended periods
Producing one or few units of a product strictly as per customer specifications
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch3 Q17. Which of the following is an example of jobbing production?
options: A cement factory running continuous production
A food company producing thousands of packaged meals daily
A pharmaceutical company producing drugs in batches
A tailor stitching clothes as per individual customer measurements
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch3 Q18. A key characteristic of jobbing production is:
options: Products are made and stocked until demand arises
The production flow is continuous and uninterrupted
Highly skilled labour is required to perform specialized jobs
Large volumes of standardized products are produced
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

options: Very short because production is fully automated
Perfectly proportionate and balanced between design and production
Disproportionate — for example, the design time may exceed the manufacturing time
Fixed and predetermined at the start of every production run
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch3 Q20. The cost in jobbing production is:
options: Calculated based on average market prices
Determined by the government regulatory authority
Fixed at the time of signing the contract
Variable and determined after completion of the product
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch3 Q21. Batch production schedules are decided according to:
options: The availability of raw materials from suppliers
Employee availability and shift timings

questions.question: Ch3 Q22. In batch production, all jobs of one batch must be:

Completed before starting the next batch of production
Completed simultaneously with the next batch

A tailor stitching a custom suit
Steel production in a continuous processing plant
Manufacturing of drugs and pharmaceuticals

They can only produce one type of product efficiently
They reduce the need for skilled labour completely

Only when raw materials are available from suppliers
Constantly based on demand forecasts on a large scale
Based on individual customer orders on a small scale

Products are varied and change according to customer orders
Products are standardized and produced on predetermined quality standards
General-purpose machines are used for a variety of products

Customized based on individual customer requirements
Varied to accommodate different customer specifications
Standardized along with the production process and sequence

options: A goldsmith making custom jewellery
A tailor stitching individual garments
A construction company building a dam
A food industry producing large-scale food based on demand forecasts
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch3 Q30. The two types of continuous production systems are:
options: Intermittent production and batch production

Batch production and project production
Mass production and process production

questions.question: Ch3 Q31. In mass production, goods are produced:

In small quantities based on specific customer orders
In batches with production halts between each run
As a single type of product with zero flexibility

questions.question: Ch3 Q32. Which of the following is an example of mass production?

Production of steel in a continuous processing plant

Producing multiple types of products with high flexibility
Producing only one specific type of product with almost zero flexibility
Producing goods strictly based on customer orders

Manufacturing of pharmaceuticals in batches

Production of steel, cement, or sugar

Unpredictable and varies with market demand
Very less because material flow is continuous
Very high due to complex and varied production processes

questions.question: Ch3 Q38. Which of the following correctly compares mass production and process production?
options: Mass production has zero flexibility; process production produces multiple product types

Both produce a variety of products with high flexibility
Mass production produces different product types in large volumes; process production produces only one product type

questions.question: Ch3 Q39. In process production, labour requirements are described as:
options: Only unskilled workers with no technical knowledge
Highly skilled workers for every stage of production
No labour required as the process is fully automated
Low-skilled labour and skilled technicians

questions.question: Ch3 Q40. Production planning and scheduling in process production:
options: Cannot be determined in advance due to unpredictable demand
Is outsourced to third-party logistics companies EM MCQ BANK
Can be decided well in advance due to continuous and standardized production
Is done randomly based on daily operational requirements

questions.question: Ch4 Q1. Production Planning and Control is best compared to which of the following in a production operation?
options: The nervous system of a production operation
The skeleton that provides structure to the organization
The marketing framework that guides customer interactions
The financial engine that drives profitability

questions.question: Ch4 Q2. The primary concern of Production Planning and Control is:
options: Managing supplier relationships and procurement contracts
Developing new product designs based on customer feedback
Delivery of products to customers or inventory stocks according to a predetermined schedule
Maximizing employee productivity and reducing absenteeism
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch4 Q3. From a long-term perspective (seven to ten years or more), production planning largely deals with:
options: Short-range utilization of labour, materials, and physical facilities
Plant construction, location, product-line design, and development
Inventory goals and wage budgets
Capital equipment budgeting and plant capacity
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

options: Capital-equipment budgeting and plant capacity
Inventory goals and wage budgets
Long-term market expansion and international growth
Plant construction and product-line development
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch4 Q5. Medium-range plans projected over a two-to-five-year period are primarily concerned with:
options: Inventory management and short-term material procurement
Daily production schedules and shift timings
Capital-equipment budgeting and plant capacity and layout
Customer order processing and dispatch management
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

Minimize the number of employees required in the production process
Maximize production output regardless of quality standards
Eliminate all forms of work-in-progress from the production system

questions.question: Ch4 Q7. Which of the following is a specific objective of Production Planning and Control? EM MCQ BANK Chapter 4: Production Planning & Control and Operations Management Systems Page 23 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: Maximizing shareholder returns through aggressive pricing
Establishing routes and schedules for work to ensure optimum utilization of raw materials, laborers, and machines
Recruiting and training skilled employees for the production line
Developing marketing campaigns to increase product demand
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch4 Q8. Production Planning and Control is essentially concerned with the control of:
options: Financial budgets and investment decisions
Customer complaints and after-sales service
Work-in-process
Marketing strategies and brand management
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch4 Q9. Which of the following is listed as an objective fulfilled by Production Planning and Control?
options: Developing new products based on emerging market trends
Managing employee salaries and compensation packages
Analyzing orders to determine raw materials and parts required for completion
Conducting market research to identify new customer segments
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

options: Dispatching
Scheduling

Follow-up

Conducting inspection of products to ensure high quality
Checking whether work proceeds according to predetermined plans

Issuing necessary orders and taking steps to ensure time targets are achieved
Fixing the timetable and quantity of work to be done
Checking work against predetermined plans and identifying variances
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

Taking steps to check whether work proceeds according to predetermined plans and identifying variances
Preparing route sheets showing the sequence of operations
Issuing requisitions for the purchase of necessary materials
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

options: Inspection — conducting check-ups of products to ensure high quality
Developing IT infrastructure for data management EM MCQ BANK
Managing customer relationship profiles and communication records
Conducting SWOT analysis for strategic planning
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

options: A marketing system for forecasting customer demand

A computerized system for planning the requirements for raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished items
A financial budgeting tool for managing production costs
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

The number of products to be manufactured based on customer demand
Financial investment plans for capital equipment

Eliminates the need for production planning entirely

questions.question: Ch5 Q1. Maintenance is best defined as:

A financial plan for replacing old equipment with new technology
A system for training employees on how to operate production machinery
A marketing strategy for promoting plant efficiency to investors
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

Maximize the speed of production at the expense of equipment longevity

Variable capacity based on daily production targets

Increased product quality and customer satisfaction

Automatically self-correct through regular use
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

Predictive maintenance, automated maintenance, and manual maintenance
Routine maintenance, emergency maintenance, and scheduled maintenance

Repairs are made after the equipment is out of order and cannot perform its normal function
Equipment is replaced entirely when it shows signs of wear
Maintenance engineers continuously monitor equipment to prevent failure

Schedule the next preventive maintenance visit immediately
Submit a detailed report to the operations manager for review

Are indifferent to the benefits of scheduling and do not feel financial justification for scheduling techniques EM MCQ BANK Chapter 5: Plant Maintenance & Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) Page 31 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
Have high production volumes and tight delivery schedules
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

Failure to replace worn-out parts and lack of lubrication
Conducting frequent preventive maintenance inspections
Using high-quality spare parts recommended by manufacturers

questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

Old and frequently breaking down
Located in remote sections of the factory

A maintenance approach that relies entirely on employee observation
An emergency maintenance approach used during production crises

Overhauling of machines, cleaning of water and other tanks, and white-washing of buildings
Emergency repairs during production breakdowns
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

Prevention is better than cure
Replace equipment before it shows any signs of wear
Fix it when it breaks

Outsourcing all maintenance activities to external specialists
Replacing all equipment on a fixed schedule regardless of condition

Inspection

questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch5 Q29. Predictive maintenance uses which of the following to predict equipment troubles before failure?

Increasing inventory turnover by 20% and reducing carbon emissions by 15%

questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q42. In the Green Mart Balanced Scorecard example, the Internal Business Processes Perspective measures include:
options: Employee training hours and number of new product ideas
Inventory turnover rate and carbon footprint reduction
Customer satisfaction scores and repeat purchase rate
Total sales revenue and net profit margin
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q43. "Strategy Mapping" was developed by Kaplan and Norton as:
options: A replacement for the Balanced Scorecard in complex organizations
An extension to the Balanced Scorecard to make implementations more successful — showing cause-and-effect relationships between objectives
A financial analysis technique for comparing departmental budgets
A standalone strategic planning tool independent of the Balanced Scorecard
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q44. A key problem with the Balanced Scorecard identified in the chapter is that:
options: It is only applicable to manufacturing organizations and not service firms
It focuses too heavily on non-financial measures at the expense of profitability
Many employees do not understand the organization's strategy and systems such as performance management are not linked to the strategy
It requires too many external benchmarks to be effective
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q45. The Balanced Scorecard helps reduce the tendency to:
options: Align internal processes with external customer requirements
Develop long-term strategic objectives for the organization
Concentrate on one measure — broadening the manager's view of performance
Focus on a broad range of measures simultaneously
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q46. Gains in one Balanced Scorecard perspective need to be considered alongside:
options: Losses that may arise in other perspectives — encouraging a holistic view
Only the financial perspective regardless of other outcomes
Government regulations and compliance requirements
Only the customer perspective to maintain competitive advantage
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q47. The main reason for the creation of Multidimensional Performance Models is:
options: Financial measures have become too complex for managers to understand
Government regulations now require multidimensional reporting from all organizations
Non-financial measures have proven to be more accurate than financial measures

Traditional financial performance systems have moved from being a performance system more to an information system aimed at satisfying external stakeholders — poorly designed to guide organizational direction EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 113 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q48. A key criticism of traditional performance systems is that managers have learned to:
options: Manage the traditional performance systems to obtain numbers that meet goals and secure bonuses — rather than managing the business itself
Ignore financial targets and focus on non-financial outcomes
Rely entirely on external benchmarks rather than internal performance data
Set overly ambitious targets to attract investor interest
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q49. Advances in technology have paradoxically created which problem for performance measurement?
options: Reduced data collection capabilities across organizations
An overload of information — vital information gets lost among excessive data
Reduced accuracy in financial reporting and ratio analysis
Inability to process complex financial calculations in real time
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q50. Service businesses face a fundamental challenge in measuring performance because:
options: Their customers, activities, and deals vary too widely — and people bring unpredictable differences in experience, skills, and motivation
Their production processes are identical to manufacturing firms
They have no financial costs that need to be measured or controlled
They are prohibited from using external benchmarks for comparison
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q51. The FIRST principle of service measurement states that service companies should:
options: Compare themselves against their own performance — rather than against poorly defined external measures
Focus primarily on comparing against external industry benchmarks
Outsource all measurement activities to specialist consultancies
Use only financial costs to measure performance variance
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q52. The SECOND principle of service measurement states that service companies must:
options: Restrict measurement to quantitative metrics and avoid qualitative data
Look deeper than their financial costs to discover and monitor the root causes of those expenses
Focus only on top-level financial costs to keep analysis simple
Compare their performance against the top three competitors in their industry
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q53. The THIRD principle of service measurement states that service companies must:
options: Replace all internal measurement with external benchmarking
Restrict measurement to a single functional area to avoid complexity
Set up broad cost-measurement systems to report and compare all expenses across functional silos — improving understanding of cross-functional trade-offs
Focus all measurement on individual employee productivity
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q54. Why is variance particularly difficult to measure in service businesses? EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 114 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: Metrics are not uniform across business units — for example one group in a call center may regard all calls on a given issue as a single case while another logs every call separately
Service businesses are too small to afford sophisticated measurement systems
Service businesses are not required to measure performance by law
Service activities are identical across all locations making comparison unnecessary
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q55. "Service-level agreements" create measurement challenges because:
options: The more types of services a business offers, the more variability it can expect in its agreements
They are always identical across all customer types and service lines
They eliminate the need for performance measurement in service firms
They require only financial metrics to assess compliance
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q56. "Internal benchmarks" are recommended over "external benchmarks" for service companies because:
options: External benchmarks are always more accurate than internal data
External benchmarks always lead to overestimation of performance variance
Internal benchmarks deliver more detailed metrics — allowing a company to find its own best practices and understand true cost drivers with full access to relevant information
Government regulations prohibit the use of external benchmarks in service firms
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q57. A "Cost Tree with Detailed Metrics" is described as:
options: A government-required reporting format for service companies
A financial statement showing total organizational expenditure

An important tool to help companies define internal benchmarks — allowing managers to compare performance of different accounts against similar metrics and calculate which improvements will have the most impact
A marketing tool for analyzing the profitability of different customer segments
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q58. "Measure Cost Drivers" as a principle of service measurement means:
options: Comparing service costs against the industry average benchmark
Outsourcing all cost analysis to specialist financial consultants
Looking at the underlying cause of each expense — such as cost per employee, incidents per employee per day, or incidents per product — rather than just the total cost
Measuring only the top-level financial costs of service delivery
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q59. "Measure Deep and Broad" as a principle of service measurement means:
options: Taking a comprehensive approach — measuring all relevant costs rather than only selected costs — because services are fungible and it is easy to shift costs to unmeasured areas
Using only external benchmarks to ensure objectivity
Restricting measurement to financial costs only
Focusing measurement on a single key cost area to maximize precision
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q60. The Performance Pyramid was developed by:
options: Kaplan and Norton in 1992
Fitzgerald and Moon in the 1990s
Lynch and Cross as a model to understand and define the links between objectives and performance measures at different levels in the organization
Porter and Miles as an extension of the competitive strategy framework
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q61. The Performance Pyramid is designed to ensure that:
options: The activities of every department, system, and business unit support the overall vision of the organization
Performance measurement is restricted to the top two levels of the organization
Only senior management is responsible for setting performance targets
Financial measures take precedence over non-financial measures at all levels
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q62. At the TOP of the Performance Pyramid is:
options: The Vision — through which the organization describes how it will achieve long-term success and competitive advantage
Business unit critical success factors in terms of market and financial measures
Day-to-day operational measures
Business operating system measures of internal processes
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q63. The SECOND level of the Performance Pyramid — the Business Unit — includes:
options: Critical success factors in terms of market-related measures and financial measures
The overall vision and long-term competitive strategy
Day-to-day operational measures of productivity and quality
Internal systems and processes needed to meet customer needs
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q64. The THIRD level of the Performance Pyramid — Business Operating Systems — includes:
options: Measures relating to internal systems and processes needed to meet the needs of customers — such as flexibility measures showing responsiveness to customer demands
Day-to-day operational measures at the shop-floor level
The overall organizational vision and mission
Critical success factors in terms of market share and financial returns
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q65. The LOWEST level of the Performance Pyramid contains:
options: Business unit critical success factors and financial targets
The organizational vision and long-term competitive strategy
Day-to-day operational measures
Internal process measures and operational flexibility metrics
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q66. In the Performance Pyramid, objectives flow in which direction?
options: Downward — cascading from the vision through to operational measures
From the bottom of the pyramid upward to the vision
In both directions simultaneously at all levels
From the left side of the pyramid to the right side
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q67. In the Performance Pyramid, measures and information flow in which direction? EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 116 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: From the bottom upward — operational measures inform higher-level performance
From the left side to the right side at each level
From right to left — from financial to non-financial
Downward from the vision to operational measures
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q68. The LEFT-hand side of the Performance Pyramid contains measures which are:
options: Predominantly non-financial and externally focused
Predominantly financial and internally focused
Strategic-level measures linked only to shareholder returns
Day-to-day operational measures only
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q69. The RIGHT-hand side of the Performance Pyramid contains measures which are:
options: Externally focused and non-financial
Related to innovation and employee development
Related to customer satisfaction and market share
Focused on the internal efficiency of the organization and predominantly financial
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q70. A limitation of the Performance Pyramid identified in the chapter is that it:
options: Tends to concentrate on only two groups of stakeholders — shareholders and customers — making it necessary to ensure measures for other stakeholders are also included
Is too complex and hierarchical for practical implementation in service firms
Focuses too heavily on financial measures at all levels
Does not include any non-financial measures of performance
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q71. CIMA's official definition of Performance Measurement describes it as:
options: A financial reporting tool for satisfying external stakeholder requirements
The process of assessing the proficiency with which a reporting entity succeeds — by the economic acquisition of resources and their efficient and effective deployment — in achieving its objectives
A human resource tool for evaluating individual employee performance
A marketing tool for measuring customer satisfaction and brand equity
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q72. Which of the following is identified as a reason why setting performance measures is "often more difficult than would first be imagined"?
options: Government regulations restrict the types of measures organizations can use
Employees always resist the introduction of new performance measurement systems
Performance measures are too expensive for small organizations to implement
Improving one objective — such as hospital waiting times — can have a negative effect on another equally important objective — such as quality of healthcare
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q73. The link between CSFs and performance measurement ensures that:
options: All departments use identical performance measures regardless of strategic priorities
Only financial CSFs are translated into measurable KPIs
Performance measures are set exclusively by external consultants

The performance measurement system ties into the overall strategy — areas where results must be satisfactory for competitive success are measured and monitored EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 117 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q74. KPIs for the CSF of "efficient production" in a cost leadership strategy could include:
options: Market share growth and brand awareness scores
Maximum kg of materials wasted and average time taken to produce one unit
Customer satisfaction scores and repeat purchase rates
Employee engagement levels and training hours
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q75. Once a performance measurement system is implemented, management must ensure that:
options: Information systems are put in place to collect data allowing performance to be measured on an ongoing basis
The system remains identical regardless of changes in the business environment
Performance measures are reviewed only at the annual board meeting
Only senior management has access to performance data
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q76. Which of the following correctly identifies the FOUR perspectives of the Balanced Scorecard with an appropriate example measure?
options: Financial — market share; Customer — carbon footprint; Internal — revenue growth; Learning — repeat purchase rate
Financial — employee training hours; Customer — net profit margin; Internal — customer satisfaction; Learning — inventory turnover
Financial — total sales revenue; Customer — customer satisfaction scores; Internal — inventory turnover rate; Learning — employee training hours
Financial — customer loyalty; Customer — profit margin; Internal — training hours; Learning — stock price
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q77. Which building block of Fitzgerald and Moon's model ensures employees are motivated to achieve standards?
options: Standards — by setting achievable and fair benchmarks
All three building blocks equally — no single block is more important
Rewards — by linking clear and desirable incentives to standard achievement
Dimensions — by providing clear goals for the business
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q78. Which of the following BEST explains why multidimensional performance models were created?
options: Technology limitations prevented accurate financial data collection

Traditional financial systems were designed primarily to satisfy external stakeholders and poorly designed to guide internal organizational direction — while managers learned to manage the numbers rather than the business
Traditional financial systems were too expensive to maintain
Government regulations required organizations to adopt non-financial reporting
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q79. In CIMA's terminology, "economic acquisition of resources" as part of performance measurement refers to:
options: Acquiring resources at minimum cost — the efficiency of resource procurement
Purchasing resources exclusively from domestic suppliers
Eliminating all non-essential resources from the production process EM MCQ BANK
Maximizing production output regardless of resource cost
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q80. Which of the following statements about the Balanced Scorecard is TRUE?
options: It is only applicable to large multinational corporations with complex operations
It was designed to replace all existing financial performance measures
It brings together a wide range of financial and non-financial measures to give managers a broader perspective — ensuring gains in one area are considered alongside losses in other areas
It focuses exclusively on internal operational efficiency
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C
